page: The Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 is a compute-intensive and high-memory virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced hardware instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The hardware allocation pairs compute capability with 336.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and integrates a 944 GB local NVMe SSD for fast transient storage.

Benchmark data reflects strong single-threaded and integer-heavy execution. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2217.0, supported by elevated single-core throughput in text processing and data compression routines such as single-threaded gzip (34.55 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.35 GB/sec). Small language model inference is equally robust, reaching 429.6 tokens per second during 135M text generation. While multi-threaded throughput and raw memory latency benchmarks such as PassMark memory align in the average to lower quartiles, raw clock speeds maintain high responsiveness on thread-limited workloads.

Resource allocation delivers an uncommon profile combining high CPU clock frequency with an extreme memory-to-core ratio of 21 GB per vCPU. This configuration is tailored for workloads requiring both per-core compute performance and substantial in-memory footprints without scaling to higher core counts. The included local NVMe SSD provides high-speed scratch space directly adjacent to compute resources.

The FX16mds_v2 is suited for electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory analytics, financial quantitative simulation, batch data processing, relational databases with extensive caching requirements, and intermediate matrix-accelerated inference tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure FX16mds_v2 virtual machine is built for workloads demanding both high single-thread processor frequency and substantial memory capacity. Powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor, the instance supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 260 MB of L3 cache, and support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. It includes 336.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 21.0 GB of memory per core, alongside a local 944 GB NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch storage. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench testing, text processing, and single-threaded data compression, though memory bandwidth benchmarks land in average ranges. Lacking dedicated GPUs, the configuration is best matched with electronic design automation tools, high-frequency computational tasks, in-memory databases, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
